# B5. Medicare among the transfers to the old {#oecd-medicare}

The paper calibrates the U.S. to its public pensions alone, as it does the UK and France: the tax rate covers
pension spending, and the design is read off the replacement rates of the public pension (appendix
{{< var p.app_US >}}). Medicare is the other large transfer to the U.S. old. This page reads it as part of the
system: its spending enters the tax rate, and since it pays every retiree the same benefit, it enters the design as
a flat component. The U.S. system is then larger and less earnings-related than in the paper.

## The calibration {#oecd-medicare-calibration}

Medicare raises the tax rate by its spending and lowers the design by its share of the transfers, which puts the
U.S. design below the UK's. Both calibrations target the same interest factor and workweek. To hold the interest
factor with the larger system the discount factor rises, the political weight of the old rises to sustain the
higher tax rate, and the taste for leisure falls a little, at every IES.

{{< include _generated/exhibits/OECD_Medicare.qmd >}}

## The counterfactuals {#oecd-medicare-rows}

The figure sets the counterfactuals of the paper's figure {{< var p.fig_US_overview >}} on the U.S. with Medicare
below those on the paper's U.S. Ageing moves the tax rate by about as much in the two, and it remains the largest
determinant at every IES. Starting from a less earnings-related design, flat benefits raise the tax rate by less
and fully earnings-related ones lower it by more; the gap between the two corners narrows, most at an IES of two.
France's income distribution lowers the tax rate by more, and France's voting patterns raise it by more; at an IES
of two, as on the paper's U.S., France's voting patterns move the tax rate by more than either corner of the
design.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
import {counterfactuals, control, ROWS_GIVEN, RHO, GIVEN_OUTCOMES} from "./assets/oa.js"
oecd = FileAttachment("_generated/data/OECD_Counterfactuals.csv").csv({typed: true})
oecdMain = oecd.filter(d => d.source === "main" && d.calibration === "commonX" && d.effect === "full")
viewof b5Out = control("radio", GIVEN_OUTCOMES, {key: "outcome", label: "Outcome", value: "tau"})
counterfactuals(oecdMain, {rows: ROWS_GIVEN, series: RHO, outcome: b5Out, width,
  facets: [{label: "U.S., pensions alone (the paper's)", filter: d => d.host === "US"},
           {label: "U.S., pensions and Medicare", filter: d => d.host === "USMedicare"}]})
```
